global_constraints.authored_claim: MapForce registers its COM server at installation. Every client machine needs MapForce plus the integration application/code.
Application is the automation entry point for navigating the object model.

Some automation methods require a visible or embedded GUI; the manual points to MapForce Server for fully unattended cross-platform mapping. This is a source claim, not Ferrule or vendor execution evidence.
Visual Studio clients reference the installed MapForce.tlb.

Documented ProgIDs are MapForce.Application (32-bit) and MapForce_x64.Application (64-bit). Client registry-view bitness affects activation; installed 32-bit and 64-bit copies require deliberate selection.
Keep object references only while needed: user actions between calls can invalidate them. Release references explicitly where required; a crashed client may leave MapForce running.
Java access depends on installed AltovaAutomation.dll, AltovaAutomation.jar, and MapForceAPI.jar; bridge/classpath/native setup is required. The Java sample calls for JDK 7 or newer.

COM Long projects to System.Int32 in .NET. Java wrappers lowercase initial method letters and expose property get/set methods; enum values correspond to COM values. These projections are not additional COM overloads.
COM failures expose IErrorInfo/HRESULT information through client-language error handling; example code is not execution evidence.
